uncertain.why: Line 1 «وَقَهَرْتَ بِهِ الموجود»: two sukun marks printed over «المو» — the upper one on the lam, the lower one sits at the mark position of the meem in the لمـ ligature (not centred over the waw). No fatha on meem and nothing else over the waw. Intended word is clearly الْمَوْجُودَ; written as the marks appear (sukun on meem) inside [؟:…]. If the lower sukun is judged to belong to the waw, read الْموْجُودَ.

Line 8 «وَتَنْصُرُ بِيَ الصالحين»: only one kasra is printed under the لحـ ligature, positioned under the lam's foot (same spot as the lam's kasra in «الصَّالِحَاتِ» p.107). Taken as the lam's kasra with the hah's kasra missing; it could instead be the hah's kasra (الصَّالحِينَ).

print_errors.note: Expected الْمَوْجُودَ: fatha on meem missing, a sukun printed on meem (or misplaced from the waw).
Expected الصَّالِحِينَ; one of the two kasras under the لحـ ligature is missing.
Printed sukun on the nun of مِنْ before hamzat al-wasl (expected مِنَ الِاعْتِرَاضِ). Kept as printed.
Fatha printed on the dal of سيدنا (expected سَيِّدِنَا, genitive after عَلَى). Same as in the parallel prayer on p.100. Kept as printed.
Both a damma (above) and a kasra (below) are printed on the final dal of مُحَمَّد and مَحْمُود; encoded as dal + damma + kasra. Same as on p.100.

notes: p109 continues prayer ١٦ (يا قهار) from p108 mid-sentence, so marker <<<ص:109+>>>; no footnotes on p109 or p112. p111 starts in the middle of the Quran quote 42:52 begun on p110: the quote is closed with ﴾ at the end of p110 and reopened with ﴿ at the start of p111 (one-line balance rule), marker <<<ص:111+>>>. Headings: «صلوات اليوم الثاني» ## (heading map), «الصلاة البرزخية», «صلاة التجلي», «صلاة الأولية والآخرية» ### (no harakat printed). Prayer numbers (٤) (٥) (٦) are list numbers at paragraph start. p112: «أعوذُ بِاللهِ…» is a larger bold centred line, written as a bold paragraph (as I did for p.102); calligraphic basmala written per §3; the flower bullet before each اللهم paragraph written as «* ». The final «يَا اللهُ، يَا اللهُ، يَا اللهُ» on p111 is in the same font as the prayer (the heavy look is the الله ligature), so not marked bold. الله with a printed case vowel written اللهُ / بِاللهِ without the font's automatic shadda/dagger. Final ى with the body font's automatic small alif written plain ى (عَلَى، حَتَّى، مُصْطَفَى، مَجْلَى، الْهَوَى، الشورى) per CONVENTIONS §2 — note that my earlier batch b27 wrote عَلَىٰ with ٰ, which contradicts §2. Quran: 7:180 printed ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ with a visible dagger alif over the ى (my b26 transcription of the same verse on p.102 omitted it — worth re-checking there); the quote ends at بِهَا with no waqf sign (Tanzil has ۖ there; quran.py flags only that). 33:56 has the small jim waqf (ۚ) after ٱلنَّبِىِّ and small round zeros on the silent alifs (ءَامَنُوا۟ صَلُّوا۟ وَسَلِّمُوا۟); مَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ written with ئِ as in Tanzil (the print shows the hamza+kasra under the tooth). Several words are printed with fewer marks than usual and kept so: الْإِيمانِ / وَالْإِيقانِ (line 2 p109, no fatha on meem/qaf; the later وَالْإِيمَانِ has it), بِأَنوَارِ (no sukun on nun), للطاعةِ, للشَّرْعِ, سيوفِكَ, الجَبَابِرَةَ (no sukun on lam), الأَعْظَمِ (p110, no sukun on lam), المُتَخَلِّقِ / المُتَعَلِّقِ / والمُتَحَقِّقِ / الحُسْنَى (no sukun on lam), والْمُتَخَلِّقِ and وعلى on p112 (no fatha on waw), آلِه / بِه / بِها / كُلِّها / ما عَلِمْنا مِنْها (p112). Hijri dates keep the printed heh+tatweel: ١٤٣٢هـ.
